doc.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Honesty and hiring regardless of color
summary: Kay says he never offers B.S., and answers why there are no black players in Diva: all he asks is that they play.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well someone paid you a compliment just today. They said that you never offer any B.S.

No. Because you know what? You live with yourself. I put my head on the bed, I know what I said. And I’m not doing that. I know exactly what I said and if I don’t like you I will be polite and say hello to you, but it’s like I’m saying hello to the floor. I don’t look at you. I go hello. Hello floor. Because I think that’s honest. I wish everybody well. I hope they make a million and stay healthy, but if you disrespect any members of my band, and Sherrie will tell you, I’ll go right after you. And one of the main stories, well we’ve heard, “well how come there’s no blacks in the band?” I said I don’t know color.

The door was open to everybody. If they didn’t come, what do you want from me? They could be green, blue, pink, whatever it is. If you can play, that’s all I ask for you to do is play. I don’t look at your color, Sherrie doesn’t look at your color. In other words you’ve got a baseball team and it’s all white, and you get a black shortstop or Oriental, and they can’t play shortstop, they throw the ball away, they do this, you’re going to lose the game. We’re not going to lose the game. We’re going to give you the best we got. That’s all I ask from my band. They don’t have to like me. They don’t have to love me. All I ask you to do is play. Give me an hour, and give Sherrie an hour of the best you’ve got. That’s all I ask you to do. After that you don’t have to talk to me if you don’t want to. You don’t have to. But we’re paying you, and you don’t have to accept a job. You don’t like the money? You don’t like this? You don’t like traveling? Don’t do it. But if you do it, do it, give me a hundred percent inside and give it to Sherrie. Because she gives a hundred percent. And that’s what we ask for. I don’t think that’s unreasonable.

Yeah. And we love everybody. We protect them, we help them in every possible way that we can. You know. And expect nothing back. I learned that. If you do something for someone, don’t expect anything back. Do it because you want to do it.
